title: Mock: 90-minute machine coding
summary: Timed 90-minute machine-coding mocks on unseen problems: stages announced by the tutor at 0:00, 0:30 and 0:55, scored on a seven-dimension rubric after mechanical checks (-race -count=20, a mutation, acceptance tests) and a probe walk-through; three passing mocks on distinct problems clear the gate.

units.title: Defending the code: walk-through, probes and re-attempts

outcomes.text: Run an unseen 90-minute machine-coding problem against the clock: API and lock model written by 0:10, Stage 1 green by 0:30, Stage 2 green by 0:55, feature freeze at 1:20, with tests written alongside the code.
Land interviewer-announced Stage 2 and Stage 3 requirements as additions behind seams chosen in the first ten minutes, and report how much stage-1 code each one changed.
Survive the tutor's mechanical checks: gofmt and vet clean, go test -race -count=20 green, a deliberate mutation caught by a test, and the acceptance checklist mostly passing.
Deliver the five-part concurrency note (shared state and owners, bounds, lifecycle, failure handling, evidence) in about two minutes, and make every claim in it match the code.

Answer machine-coding probes (10× load, slow or panicking dependency, lock order, next requirement, test quality, why not channels or sync.Map) with a specific mechanism, a number where one exists, and the condition under which the answer flips.
Score your own mock on the seven-dimension rubric within one level of the tutor, and apply the overall rule including the Stage 1 hard floor.
Turn each below-meets mock into a targeted re-attempt on a different problem, using the mock log's top gaps.
